Two things that bother me at FPS games is that handguns usually are limited to being your weapon of last resort (barring exceptions such as the revolver from Half-Life 2 or That Gun from Fallout/Fallout:New Vegas), while at the same time, rapid-fire miniguns or machine guns typically turn all enemies into bullet sponges that can take over a thousand projectiles to the face and still won't die.

Long story short, are there any games that either/or have a) pistols or revolvers that actually don't force you to empty an entire magazine into the enemy before the latter stops twitching - handguns with an actual BANG behind them, and have b) where going full auto onto an enemy actually has the same devastating effect on it as firing a shotgun while the barrel rests against its head has?
Games with rewarding handguns and/or rapid-fire guns?
Rainbow Six Siege. Also, any battlefield on hardcore. ARMA was good, but I haven't played in a long time.

The issue with full auto guns in game is that in real life they pack as much punch as the handgun or rifle so 2-3 to the chest and the person is down immediately and dead location not mattering so much. They are meant to cause people to take cover or to mow down large numbers. Add in that in a game you work on a health bar system and outside of the head a hand shot is as good as a shot to the heart. So things turn into DPS numbers, one hit one kill is often reserved for slow to fire, fast firing is low damage but high DPS, pistols being a default weapon means you use others as upgrades and if they were not better why would you upgrade?

You would need a game where it is almost 1 shot one kill with any weapon except the default melee that they love to make a one hit kill, or something that really tracks where you hit and cranks up the damage. The location would play more if it is humans and they wear body armor as a chest shot from a shotgun could do less damage then a leg from a pistol.

I'm going to go into way more detail then needed here to explain the issue with fallout new vegas so feel free to stop reading here.

Fallout new vegas suffers from their Damage Threshold system where damage is directly subtracted from the damage of the gun. so If you have a gun that does 10 damage and armor with a DT of 5 the gun only does 5 damage. As a result fast shooters, and shotguns are weak since they are low damage per projectile. Grab some low tier power armor and you subtract 22 form any damage number.

There are only 2 smg's that will now do more then one damage per bullet (I'm ignoring perks, and energy weapons for ease here) one does 4 (.45 ammo) the other 14 (12.7mm ammo). Shotguns will all do damage based on the number of pellets meaning the default ammo ranges from 7 to 14 with the 14 you are not likely to hit with all 14 past 3 feet. go heavy weapons high fire rate and you can get 1, 1, 4, 8, 14; those last three are 10mm, .357, .44 so only one is really even feasible as a primary weapon. What this means is that a gun with 23 or less damage will do 1 damage per bullet, a gun with 24 damage will do 2 that is a 100% boost in damage per bullet, find something with 30 and you get 8 damage or 800% of a 23.

This is why I tend to always play as a sniper so I can do decent damage with a hit, otherwise you may as well just find a 9mm smg, 10mm smg, and something that hits hard like my rifles for when you run out of ammo for the first two. sneak attacks do an extra 50% damage or something so with that 30 damage weapon you do 8 base or sneak for 23 (45-22), meaning a sneak is not 50% more (that would be 12) it is 287.5% if the base damage.

This means a sniper rifle vs minigun; the sniper does 45 base or 23 damage on our dummy to the minigun's 12 base or 1 on our dummy. Say we are closing from mid range (close for the sniper, long for the mini) we will call it 6 seconds for the baddy to close who is going to melee pop us in one hit, the sniper will get 3 shots all likely to hit at 23 damage so 69 damage, the minigun will get 120 shots (that is a lot of ammo) or 120 damage nearly double the damage but realistically the spread is going to reduce that down to comparable damage.
